purpose: Miconazole nitrate 2% is used to treat common fungal infections of the skin, such as athlete's foot, jock itch, and ringworm. It can also help with yeast infections when used in vaginal forms. It relieves the itching, burning, cracking, and scaling that these infections cause.
how_it_works: Miconazole works by attacking and destroying the outer protective layer (called the cell membrane) of the fungus. Without that protective layer, the fungus cannot survive or spread. This stops the infection and allows your skin to heal.
common_side_effects: Most people tolerate this medication well. Some people may notice mild burning, stinging, redness, or irritation right where they apply it. These effects are usually mild and go away on their own. If irritation gets worse or does not go away, let your doctor or pharmacist know.
warnings: Do not use this medication near your eyes, nose, or mouth unless your doctor tells you to. If your skin condition does not improve after 2 to 4 weeks of treatment, see your doctor because you may need a different medication. Do not use on children under 2 years old without a doctor's advice. If you are pregnant or breastfeeding, check with your doctor before using, especially the vaginal form. Stop using and call your doctor if you develop severe redness, swelling, or blistering.
typical_dosing: For skin infections like athlete's foot or ringworm, apply a thin layer to the affected area and the skin right around it, usually twice a day (morning and night). For athlete's foot, use it for 4 weeks. For jock itch and ringworm, use it for 2 weeks. Always wash and dry the area well before applying. Keep using it for the full recommended time even if it starts to feel better sooner, to make sure the infection is fully gone.
